headline: Yellowstone Entrance and Western History Access
reservation: Cody itself requires no entry permit, but Yellowstone National Park requires a separate entrance fee and may implement reservation systems during peak seasons. Museums like the Buffalo Bill Center of the West offer multi-day tickets; check the official site for current pricing and seasonal rodeo schedules.

days.title: Frontier History and Western Lore

stops.name: Buffalo Bill Center of the West
stops.detail: Visit this complex of five museums covering Plains Indian cultures, firearms, and regional natural history.

stops.name: Old Trail Town
stops.detail: Walk through a collection of authentic 19th-century frontier cabins and historic structures from the Old West.

days.driving: Allow 10 minutes; sights are located within or very near town limits.
days.note: Old Trail Town is outdoors; comfortable walking shoes are necessary for uneven dirt paths.

days.title: North Fork Valley Vistas
days.start: Suggested: 8:30 AM from Buffalo Bill Dam

stops.name: Buffalo Bill State Park
stops.detail: Stop at the reservoir for views of the dramatic rock formations and the Shoshone River canyon.

stops.name: Buffalo Bill Cody Scenic Byway
stops.detail: Drive the North Fork corridor toward the mountains, watching for bighorn sheep and elk along the river.

days.driving: Allow 2–3 hours round trip; conditions vary with weather and wildlife traffic.
days.note: Strong winds are common around the reservoir; keep car doors secured at overlooks.

days.title: High Country Exploration
days.start: Suggested: 8 AM from Chief Joseph Scenic Byway

stops.name: Dead Indian Pass
stops.detail: Ascend to the overlook for panoramic views of the Sunlight Basin and the Absaroka Mountains.

stops.name: Shoshone National Forest
stops.detail: Access established trailheads for high-elevation hiking in the nation's first national forest.

days.driving: Allow 3–4 hours; steep grades and switchbacks require careful driving.
days.note: Verify road status at Dead Indian Pass during early summer or autumn as snow is frequent.

intel.title: Museum and Trailhead Stays
intel.text: The Buffalo Bill Center has ample paved parking, but downtown spots fill quickly during the summer rodeo season. High-country trailheads have limited gravel spaces; arrive early to secure a spot.

intel.title: Mountain Connectivity
intel.text: Cellular service is reliable within Cody but disappears rapidly once you enter the Shoshone National Forest or North Fork corridor. Download maps and satellite data for any off-road navigation.

intel.title: Last Chance Fuel
intel.text: Fill your tank in Cody before heading west toward Yellowstone or north on the Chief Joseph Scenic Byway. There are long stretches of mountain road without any services or fuel stations.

intel.title: Yellowstone Gate Logistics
intel.text: The East Entrance is a 50-mile drive from town. Allow significant extra time for entrance lines and wildlife-related traffic jams which can occur at any time of day.

intel.title: Seasonal Road Closures
intel.text: The Beartooth Highway and Chief Joseph Scenic Byway are subject to closures due to snow even in summer months. Check WYDOT for real-time updates before attempting these high-mountain routes.

plan.arrival: Arrive at Yellowstone Regional Airport (COD) and pick up your vehicle. Cody is a compact gateway; check into your lodging and stock up on bear spray and water downtown.
plan.vehicle: A high-clearance vehicle is recommended for forest service roads; check rental policies regarding travel on unpaved routes.
plan.goldenHour: Buffalo Bill Reservoir for sunset views against the Absaroka range, subject to local cloud cover.
